ideas.description: Start from the E019 Muon recipe (commit 45b511c): Muon on the 9 group 3x3 convs, lr 0.24, momentum 0.6, Nesterov, 3 NS steps in bf16; SGD for BN/biases/head; lookahead-EMA. Change only the epoch count, from 8.5 to 7.0. Rescale the LR, lookahead and EMA schedules to the new total step count, the same way the recipe already does (as in E007). Leave the Muon step code eager and unchanged so the run measures the Muon accuracy-vs-epochs slope with no confound. Log per-seed accuracies.
ideas.expected: Time about 6.55-6.70 s (8.04 x 7/8.5 = 6.62 s; the Muon per-step overhead scales with steps), i.e. -8 to -9% vs A1a's 7.22 s. Accuracy 0.752-0.760 (0.7663 minus ~1.5 epochs at a 0.5-1.0 pp/epoch slope). If >=0.756 it is a new tip with margin, and H5 is refuted on time-to-75 as well. If 0.750-0.756, the next step is 7.5 epochs or the cheaper Muon step (I023). Below 0.750 means Muon's slope is steeper than SGD's at short schedules.

ideas.hypothesis: H5.2 (new, under H5): Muon's +0.82 s over SGD (E019, ~2 ms/step) comes mostly from CPU launch overhead of eager per-parameter Newton-Schulz while the GPU idles, not from NS FLOPs (~60 GFLOP/step, <0.5 ms in bf16). Batching and compiling the step removes most of it.
ideas.description: On E019's recipe at 8.5 epochs, change only the Muon update implementation and keep the math. Group filters by identical [out, in*9] shape (conv2/conv3 of each group, so 6 of 9 params, plus the 3 conv1s individually) and stack each group into one batched tensor. Run the 3 NS iterations as batched bmm in bf16, together with momentum/Nesterov, normalization and the weight update, inside one torch.compile'd function (mode max-autotune-no-cudagraphs or default), warmed up in build on synthetic gradients. Instrumentation only: record per-step wall time of the optimizer phase on one trial, and NVML power at >=10 Hz (observational, which also covers H2.4.1 for this recipe).
ideas.expected: Time 7.30-7.55 s (from 8.04 s, recovering 60-90% of the 0.82 s Muon overhead). Accuracy 0.762-0.769: unchanged within numerics noise (~0.3 pp on the mean). If the overhead falls by <30%, NS is energy-bound rather than launch-bound, and the fix is fewer NS steps or lower-rank orthogonalization instead. Stacks directly on I022 (the predicted 7.0-epoch time would be ~6.0-6.1 s).

ideas.description: Port the two-stage 24->32 px progressive schedule to the E019 Muon recipe. 8.0 total epochs: epochs 0-3 at 24 px, epochs 4-7 at 32 px, no 28 px phase. Use the E006 operator: flip + translate-2 at 32 px, then F.interpolate(bilinear, antialias=True) to 24 px, with AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) as the final pool. Rescale the LR/EMA/lookahead schedules to the step count. Keep the Muon step eager as in E019. In build, compile and warm up both train shapes and the 32 px eval, so nothing recompiles in timed code.
ideas.expected: Time 6.2-6.5 s: 4x0.485 + 4x0.848 + ~0.2 overhead = 5.53 s for the SGD part, plus ~0.78 s of eager Muon overhead over ~392 steps. That is -10 to -14% vs A1a. Accuracy 0.754-0.761: an SGD estimate of ~0.746-0.749 for this schedule (between E006 and E007), plus ~1.1 pp from Muon. If >=0.756 it becomes the tip and is the base for the compiled-Muon stack. If Muon's gain shrinks to <0.5 pp under low-res epochs, Muon and progressive resizing overlap (both buy early-phase efficiency).

ideas.description: On E019's Muon recipe at 8.5 epochs, raise the batch size from 1024 to 2000. Scale the SGD param groups (BN/bias/head) by the same kilostep rule as E010, and scale the EMA/lookahead schedule by the step count. Keep Muon lr 0.24 and momentum 0.6, which are airbench94_muon's own settings at bs 2000. Warm up the new shapes in build. This tests whether Muon removes the large-batch penalty SGD showed (E010: -0.81 pp) while halving the per-step Muon overhead.
ideas.expected: Time 7.55-7.70 s (E019's 8.04 s minus half of the ~0.82 s Muon overhead; the conv work is unchanged per E010). Accuracy 0.756-0.766: a smaller penalty than SGD's -0.8 pp if Muon tolerates large batches. A loss of <=0.3 pp makes bs 2000 the preferred Muon batch, since it halves the optimizer overhead. A loss of >=0.7 pp confirms that updates per epoch are binding (H1.6) for both optimizers.

ideas.description: On E019's Muon recipe (8.5 epochs), replace every exact GELU with nn.GELU(approximate='tanh'). Change nothing else, and recompile/warm up in build. Running this on the Muon base means the expected ~1% saving can be kept even with perturbation noise, since that base has 1.3 pp of margin.
ideas.expected: Time -0.8 to -1.5% vs E019 (about 7.93-7.98 s), because the fused BN+act kernels use less energy (E003: SiLU saved 2.2%). Accuracy within 0.25 pp of 0.7663. If time falls by <0.5%, the erf cost is not the energy driver and elementwise micro-tuning is done.

ideas.description: Explore Muon hyperparameters, which came untuned from CIFAR-10 airbench94 (bs 2000). On the I022 recipe (Muon, 7.0 epochs), change only the Muon momentum from 0.6 to 0.85 (Nesterov kept, lr 0.24 unchanged). Higher momentum is the usual Muon setting at smaller batches, and bs 1024 gives each step half the gradient averaging of bs 2000. If I022 has not run yet, run this at 8.5 epochs against E019 instead.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged vs its base (±0.5%). Accuracy -0.3 to +0.5 pp vs its base. A gain of >=0.3 pp buys ~0.3-0.5 epochs (~4-6% of time) at no cost. A loss means 0.6 is near-optimal, so the next lever is lr, not momentum.

structured_output.summary:
The six new ideas follow up on E019. Switching the group convs to Muon gave +1.14 pp accuracy (0.7663) but cost +0.82 s (8.04 s). That swing makes Muon the main lever, with enough margin to spend on time cuts.

**Exploit ideas (four)**
- **Muon at 7.0 epochs (I022, priority 5).** Measures Muon's accuracy-per-epoch slope. Predicted ~6.6 s, which would beat A1a by about 8% if accuracy holds at ≥0.753.
- **Batched, compiled Newton-Schulz step (I023, priority 4).** Tests a new hypothesis, H5.2: the 0.82 s Muon overhead comes from CPU kernel-launch cost, not from the matrix math. Predicted 7.3-7.55 s at 8.5 epochs, and it stacks on the other Muon runs.
- **Muon with the two-stage 24→32 px schedule (I024, priority 4).** 4 epochs at 24 px then 4 at 32 px (no 28 px phase). Predicted 6.2-6.5 s at 0.754-0.761.
- **Exact GELU → tanh approximation on the Muon base (I026, priority 2).** About 1% time, cheap enough to keep now that Muon gives margin.

**Explore ideas (two)**
- **Muon at batch size 2000 (I025, priority 3).** Halves the per-step Muon overhead and tests whether Muon avoids the large-batch accuracy loss SGD showed in E010.
- **Muon momentum 0.6 → 0.85 (I027, priority 2).** The current Muon settings were tuned for CIFAR-10 at batch size 2000.

**Queue and tree housekeeping**
- Nothing was dropped: every earlier queued idea is already done or dropped.
- Three open hypotheses were tested only with SGD: H2.1.4, H2.7.1 and H2.8.1. They should now be rerun on Muon, and I024 starts that.
- H5 should be marked refuted once I022 confirms that Muon also reduces time-to-75%.
- H5.2 needs to be added to the tree under H5.
